evidence.note: After the PaymentIntent full-flow test, the agent revised cards.py (two consecutive edits) and restarted to verify decline + invalid-PAN handling — a design revision driven by a failing/unexpected check rather than pressing on.

Sustained diagnosis of a card-decline failure; agent correctly identified that failures were partly due to a stale server process holding port 8000 (kill stale procs, find python via /proc, fresh restart) — distinguishing environment root cause from code logic instead of symptom-patching.

Re-verified decline/bad-PAN then exercised the deep traps (idempotency error replay, webhook retry, manual capture, 4xx-stop) with no further edits, indicating the root-cause fix held; but corrections stayed localized to one module with no cross-endpoint propagation or structural pivot visible.

reasoning: The visible arc shows the agent stopping on a failing card-decline test, editing the relevant module, and diagnosing a genuine root cause (stale server process vs. code) before re-verifying — matching the level-5 anchor of diagnosing and fixing the root cause for the failing case and moving on. There is no evidence of higher-anchor behavior (treating a divergence as a contract signal and propagating fixes across related endpoints, or structural pivots to idempotency/webhook/state-machine design). Confidence is medium because the trajectory file is a thin index of step titles without message or observation content, so finer signals of model-updating may be unobservable.
